locator: Store currency
quote: This is the primary currency that your customers will use when making purchases on your store. You can select any currency from the available options in your store settings based on your customer base's location.

locator: Payout currency
quote: The payout currency refers to the currency that Shopify Payments uses to deposit money into your bank account. This depends on the location of your store, and your bank account must generally be in the same country as your store.

locator: Changing your store currency

locator: Impact of changing store currency
quote: Before you change your store currency, review the following impact of this change on your store:

locator: Impact of changing store currency
quote: * The currency of your product prices and discount rates update automatically, but not the amount. For example, if you change from USD to CAD, then a product that was listed as 20 USD is now listed as 20 CAD.

locator: Impact of changing store currency
quote: * The amount and currency of shipping rates aren't updated automatically.

locator: Impact of changing store currency
quote: * Gift cards with remaining balances in the old currency will no longer work.

locator: Impact of changing store currency
quote: * Apps that have currency requirements different from the new currency won't work after the currency has been changed.

locator: Impact of changing store currency
quote: * Changing your store currency might affect your reports, due to currency rate fluctuations and the report update cycles.

locator: Impact of changing store currency
quote: * Changing your store currency might affect orders with pending payments.

locator: Impact of changing store currency
quote: * Refunds processed after a currency change will also be affected by the currency change due to the difference in values.

locator: Impact of changing store currency
quote: * If you use a payment provider other than Shopify Payments, then the currencies of all of your markets will update to match the new currency.

locator: Impact of changing store currency
quote: * If you're using Paypal Express, then your new currency might not be supported.

locator: Impact of changing store currency
quote: * Managed Markets is deactivated if you change your store currency. To continue using Managed Markets, your store currency must remain set to the required currency for your region.

quote: If you don't have a bank account set up in the currency that was used to pay for an order, then the payout is sent to your default bank account.

locator: Replace a bank account, step 5
quote: You can't change the country or currency of the account that you want to add. The account that you want to add must be in the same currency as the account that you're replacing.

locator: Delete a bank account, step 4
quote: Payouts are deposited into your default account if an account in that currency isn't added.

locator: Handling orders in non-account currencies
quote: If you receive an order in a currency that you don't have a specific bank account for, then the funds are converted to your default account's currency.

locator: Refunds in multiple currencies
quote: Refunds are processed in the same currency as the original order. The refund is deducted from the bank account in that currency.

locator: Refunds in multiple currencies
quote: If you don't have a bank account in the original order's currency, then the refund is deducted from your default bank account in your domestic currency.

locator: Chargebacks in multiple currencies
quote: Chargebacks are handled in the same currency as the original order. If a customer disputes a charge, then the chargeback amount is deducted from the bank account in that currency.

locator: Refunds
quote: Refunds are always issued to a customer in the currency that they used to pay for the order.

locator: Refunds
quote: * If the currency needs to be converted for the refund, then the current currency rate, and not the currency rate at the time of the order, is used in the conversion.

locator: Setting up currencies for markets, Note
quote: To process payments in multiple currencies, your store must use Shopify Payments or Adyen as its payment processor. If you use a different provider, then customers in all markets pay in your store's default currency.

locator: Setting up currencies for markets
quote: Each market can have a currency customization that determines what currency is displayed to customers in that market. When a customer visits your store, their market is identified and prices are displayed in the currency configured for that market.

locator: Currency inheritance
quote: [Submarkets](/manual/markets/getting-started/submarkets) inherit the currency customization of their parent market by default. If you add a currency customization to a submarket, then it overrides the parent's currency.

locator: Add a currency customization to a market, step 5
quote: * Select **Dynamic** to automatically convert prices. Prices are converted using the current market exchange rate, updated regularly. The currency conversion fee is included in the price that's displayed to your customer.

locator: Add a currency customization to a market, step 5
quote: * Select **Manual** to set a fixed exchange rate. The conversion fee isn't added to prices displayed to your customer. Instead, the fee is reflected in your payouts.

locator: Currency for single-country markets
quote: When you create a market for a single country, the market's currency is automatically set to that country's local currency. For example, creating a Japan market automatically sets the currency to JPY. You can change this to any supported currency.

locator: Currency for multi-country markets
quote: When you create a market with multiple countries, the default currency is set to your store's base currency, and local currencies are activated. This means each country in the market displays prices in its own local currency, automatically converted from the market's base currency.

locator: Currency for multi-country markets
quote: If you deactivate local currencies for a multi-country market, then prices in the market's base currency are displayed for all customers in that market, regardless of their location.

locator: Fees and multi-entity stores
quote: If your store uses multiple business entities with Shopify Payments accounts in different countries, then the conversion fee depends on which entity processes the payment. If the customer's payment currency matches the entity's payout currency, then no conversion fee is charged.

locator: Supported currencies
quote: Shopify Payments supports several currencies for international selling. The currencies available to you depend on your store's location and your payment processor.

locator: Supported currencies
quote: If a country's local currency isn't supported by Shopify Payments, then prices in the market's base currency are displayed to customers in that country instead.

locator: Refunds in foreign currencies
quote: * **At the time of purchase**: The customer pays in their local currency. The payment is converted to your payout currency using the exchange rate at that time.

locator: Refunds in foreign currencies
quote: * **At the time of refund**: You issue a refund in the customer's original currency. The refund amount is converted back to your payout currency using the exchange rate at that time.

locator: Refunds with manual exchange rates
quote: If you use manual exchange rates, then refunds are still processed at the current market exchange rate at the time of the refund, not at the manual rate you set.

locator: Chargebacks
quote: Chargebacks follow the same logic as refunds. The amount debited from your account in your payout currency is based on the exchange rate at the time of the chargeback, not the time of the original transaction.
